purpose: The anti-overfit variation for BUG-IFRAME-SELECTOR. Widens the character set beyond fixture 03's dot-in-id and quote-in-name to apostrophes, brackets, parentheses, backslashes and spaces, and exercises the TITLE branch (which had never been escaped at all) as well as the id and name branches.
targeted_defect: BUG-IFRAME-SELECTOR (variation): frameSelectorFor() has four branches - id, name, title, src - and each interpolated raw. Escaping only the two characters fixture 03 happens to use would leave the rest broken.
lane_note: Playwright only: the acceptance is that the emitted selector RESOLVES to exactly one frame in a real engine. jsdom has no frame-locator equivalent, so it could only compare selector strings - which is the test this ticket explicitly must not be reduced to.

expect_controls.why: Captured at all - i.e. the walker descended a same-origin frame whose title is full of metacharacters.

frame_selectors_must_resolve.why: The real contract, asserted in test_capture_contract.py by handing each emitted selector back to the browser. A selector that resolves to zero frames is a control the crawl claimed to capture and replay cannot reach; one that resolves to several is worse, because it binds to the wrong frame silently.
